definitions.explanation: The closing period of the summer season, typically late August to early September in Japan. A phrase with strong emotional resonance in Japanese culture, evoking nostalgia, the passage of time, and a bittersweet sense of endings.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}の{終|お}わりが{近|ちか}づいている。
examples.english: The end of summer is approaching.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}の{終|お}わりに{花火大会|はなびたいかい}があった。
examples.english: There was a fireworks festival at the end of summer.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}の{終|お}わりの{夕暮|ゆうぐ}れは、どこか{寂|さび}しさを{感|かん}じさせる。
examples.english: The twilight at the end of summer somehow evokes a feeling of loneliness.

notes:
A set phrase frequently used in literature, songs, and everyday conversation to mark the transition from summer to autumn. In Japanese culture, the end of summer carries particularly strong emotional associations: the end of school holidays, the fading of cicada songs, the last fireworks festivals, and the shift toward cooler weather. It is a common theme in songs, novels, and anime.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {夏|なつ}の{終|お}わりの{空|そら}: the sky at the end of summer
- {夏|なつ}の{終|お}わりを{告|つ}げる: to signal the end of summer
- {夏|なつ}の{終|お}わりの{思|おも}い{出|で}: memories from the end of summer

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {晩夏|ばんか}: late summer — the Sino-Japanese equivalent; more literary
- {残暑|ざんしょ}: lingering summer heat — the heat that continues into early autumn
- {夏|なつ}の{始|はじ}まり: beginning of summer — the opposite seasonal transition
